On the associated media player card the Lounge Sonos correctly displays as being in 'TV' mode.

2022.2.8

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2021.11 (pretty sure only happening since 1/1/2022)

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/

My working theory is that the `cannot reach None` messages appear when there's a race condition during subscription creation where multiple attempts are sent simultaneously. This causes a reject and loss of the listening address on the subscription instance (hence the `None`). The 2022.3 release will guard against this, but we'll need to see if that's the root cause after release (or during beta).

A side note is that I have never encountered this issue in local testing (with a soundbar & surrounds) and I tend to hammer the system with lots of intentional failure scenarios. Hopefully we can find a common theme soon.

If you have more than one Sonos device wired via ethernet, you **must** make sure you're not creating a network loop with improper STP handling. If you're unsure of how to verify this, an alternative is to explicitly disable the wifi on all but one of your wired speakers using the native Sonos app. Ideally, keep the wifi enabled on the best-positioned wired speaker.

I've tried reproducing some of the scenarios in this issue and have encountered transient losses of connectivity, but the system always seems to recover in the matter of a minute or two. For example, moving back and forth between wired (using SonosNet with **one** wired speaker) and pure wifi (across multiple APs) will cause the speakers to become unavailable for a short time (and sometimes reboot?). However I've never had a speaker randomly disappear from the network indefinitely like in some of the setups described above.

I'll keep testing to see if I can reproduce these problems, but many of the clues are hinting at local network setup quirks.

Add one or two more players to your setup, reboot them all or just ungroup them via the app and note that one after the other becomes unresponsive. comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
There are two possible issues going on here:
#### Message is _"cannot reach <IP_ADDRESS>"_
This means the Sonos device(s) cannot connect back to your Home Assistant host on port 1400 (default) in order to deliver subscription events. The HA host will open a listening port and if we don't receive any messages then this warning is displayed. This is almost always caused by a networking issue in your local setup and is not a bug in the integration, but a setup issue.

#### Message _"cannot reach None"_
This implies something went wrong when creating the subscription and we're not actually listening for subscription events for some reason. This is always unexpected and what we're trying to track down here. I've added several fixes in the last few releases which attempt to address this issue, but it seems that some users might still be encountering this in 2022.5. I'm looking for confirmation of that here.

If your problem is the latter, debug logs, diagnostics, and answering the questions in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/66717#issuecomment-1048122648 would be useful.
